title: Why Some Representatives Produce Three Times What Others Do
content:
###  **A Gap Wider Than Most Roles** 

In most jobs, the difference between a strong performer and an average one is meaningful but modest. In field work it is not modest. The best representative on a team will routinely produce several times what an average one does, working the same hours in the same neighborhoods. 

###  **It Is Not Door Count** 

The obvious assumption is that top performers simply knock more doors. They usually do not. Door counts across a team tend to be fairly similar. 

The difference is what happens in the thirty seconds after a door opens. 

###  **What Top Performers Do Differently** 

They lead with something relevant to that specific house rather than a rehearsed opening. They read whether the homeowner has thirty seconds or five minutes and adjust immediately. They ask about the home rather than talking about the company. And they are comfortable enough that the homeowner relaxes, which is when real conversations start. 

None of that is scriptable. It comes from people who are naturally good at conversation being placed in a role where that is the whole job. 

###  **Why This Shapes How We Hire** 

If the performance gap were small, hiring for availability would be reasonable. Because the gap is enormous, being selective about who ends up in a territory is not a nicety — it is the entire difference between a program that works and one that does not.
